title: Studying Protein Function and the Role of Altered Protein Expression by Antibody Interference and Three-dimensional Reconstructions
protocol: Reconstitute the lyophilized active motif powder in sterile H2O to a final concentration of 2 µg/µl.
Tap carefully for mixing.
Prepare small aliquots, such as 12 µl each, and store them at -20 °C.
Seed mammalian cells like HEK293 cells or primary neurons on a 24 well plate in 500 µl growth medium including antibiotics.
Culture the cells at appropriate conditions (humidified, 5% CO2 and 37 °C) until the cells are approximately 50% confluent.
When using neurons, seed the cells at low density and use only the two middle rows of the 24 well plate.
Each well will have an empty counterpart to harbor the medium during incubation.
Culture neurons until the desired developmental stage is reached and change approximately 25-50% of the medium twice a week.
Prepare Chariot complex by diluting 0.1-2 µg of the protein of interest or corresponding antibody, along with the control protein or control antibody in 50 µl of PBS per reaction.
Mix thoroughly.
Spin down the mixture.
Dilute 2 µl Chariot stock solution in 50 µl PBS using separate tubes to avoid self-association of Chariot.
Mix and spin the diluted Chariot solution.
Transfer the diluted POI or antibody to the Chariot dilution by pipetting.
Mix and spin the mixture containing POI or antibody with Chariot.
Incubate the mixture for 30 min at room temperature.
Dilute the Chariot complexes in 100 µl pre-warmed growth medium (37 °C, no additives).
Remove the medium from cells and wash once using pre-warmed PBS containing 0.5 mM MgCl2 and CaCl2.
Apply the diluted Chariot complex solution to the cells and rock gently for even distribution.
Grow the cells under standard conditions for 1 hr.
Add serum to a final concentration of 10%.
When using neurons, add the medium from step 4.1 back after washing.
Grow the cells for 1 to 2 more hours depending on cargo size and properties.
Process cells for analysis as usual.
Take z-stacks of cells and/or cell compartments using a laser scanning microscope with approximately 0.25-0.5 µm distance between layers.
Open the lsm-file in Imaris.
Use Display Adjustment to contrast each channel until the brightest structures reach saturation.
Click on the Add new Surfaces icon.
Select Segment only a Region of Interest from the wizard options.
Adjust the margins of the selection box to fit the object of interest, considering all three dimensions (x, y, and z).
Enlarge or adjust the shape of the selection box as necessary to ensure all required structures are embedded.
Select the appropriate channel for reconstruction.
Set the Surface Area Detail Level or sphere diameter appropriately.
Choose either Absolute Intensity or Local Contrast based on signal characteristics.
Adjust settings separately for each structure of interest.
Reconstruct the structure using the Thresholding tool.
Complete the reconstruction by clicking the green arrow button.
Cut and remove surfaces as required using the pencil tool.
Tilt the image to cut objects in the north-south direction.
Obtain volume, area, and intensity measurements for each surface.
Select Statistics, Detailed Statistics, and Average Values.
(Optional) Select 'Statistic Coded' instead of 'Base' under the color tab.
